paragraphs: Shapley values describe how features contribute to a model’s decisions, but calculating them exactly generally requires exponentially many model evaluations as the number of features grows. Randomized estimators make this more manageable. The paper addresses a theoretical gap surrounding KernelSHAP, a widely used estimator whose guarantees had remained unresolved even though related methods already had established bounds.

The authors develop a common framework covering KernelSHAP and related estimators, including approaches that sample with or without replacement. They prove guarantees for finite sample sizes across this framework. This provides what they describe as the first theoretical guarantees for KernelSHAP, while making tradeoffs between estimators easier to analyze within the same mathematical setting.

Experiments on small and medium dimensional datasets compare estimates against exact Shapley values for decision trees, finding low mean squared error with modest sample counts. Separate implementation improvements support higher dimensional datasets. Tests on MNIST and CIFAR10 report consistently better results than the KernelSHAP library, connecting the theoretical framework to practical estimation improvements.
neurips-2025-a-unified-framework-for-pro.tldr: A unified framework supplies finite-sample guarantees for KernelSHAP and related estimators, alongside practical improvements for estimating feature contributions.

paragraphs: A language model can know how to answer a question yet lose accuracy when the surrounding context contains coherent but irrelevant material. This paper studies that vulnerability by generating distractions that adapt to the model being tested. The original question and answer remain unchanged, so the stress test focuses on how additional context affects performance.

The method uses tree search guided by model behavior to develop challenging distractions. This makes the generation process responsive to observed weaknesses, addressing the limited effectiveness of fixed templates and retrieval-based distractions against contemporary models. Across four benchmarks, the resulting distractions produce an average performance drop exceeding 45% for the mainstream models evaluated.

The authors also compare ways to reduce the problem. Prompt optimization provides limited gains, whereas post-training approaches such as DPO substantially improve contextual robustness. They interpret the findings as evidence of inconsistent reasoning under distraction rather than missing knowledge. The contribution therefore includes both a stronger testing procedure and evidence about which interventions helped in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-adaptive-distraction-probin.tldr: Model-guided tree search generates irrelevant context that sharply reduces tested LLM performance, while post-training improves resistance more than prompt optimization.

paragraphs: This paper turns random forests into an autoencoding system: one part compresses information into a lower dimensional representation, and another maps that representation back to the input space. The authors use results from nonparametric statistics and spectral graph theory to construct an embedding that optimally represents relationships in the data according to their formulation.

A central contribution is making the compressed representation reversible through a decoder. The paper develops exact and approximate decoding methods using constrained optimization, split relabeling, and nearest neighbors regression. These methods draw on the splits already learned by the forest’s individual trees, establishing a reconstruction procedure tied to the ensemble’s existing structure.

The decoders have universal consistency guarantees under common regularity assumptions, so the theoretical claim is conditional on those assumptions. The approach works with both supervised and unsupervised forests, supporting examination of conditional or joint distributions. Experiments across tabular, image, and genomic data illustrate uses in visualization, compression, clustering, and denoising, showing how a forest’s representation can support tasks beyond its original predictions.
neurips-2025-autoencoding-random-forests.tldr: Random forests can support low-dimensional encoding and reconstruction, with conditional consistency guarantees and applications from visualization to denoising.

paragraphs: Online reinforcement learning from human feedback must gather useful preference information while improving a model. This paper examines how much feedback that process requires when the reward function spans a large range. The authors identify exponential dependence on this range in existing online RLHF algorithms, including methods with active exploration and those using passive exploration.

That dependence becomes especially problematic when preferences are heavily skewed, such as questions with objectively correct answers. The proposed algorithm, SE-POPO, uses preference-based exploration and achieves sample complexity that grows polynomially with the reward range. The paper presents this as the first such result, resolving an open problem about avoiding the exponential dependence.

The theoretical analysis establishes favorable sample-complexity bounds relative to existing exploration algorithms. Empirical evaluations also find SE-POPO more sample-efficient than exploratory and non-exploratory baselines across two principal RLHF application scenarios and public benchmarks. The significance is a change in how feedback requirements scale, accompanied by evidence that the algorithm’s statistical advantage is useful in the evaluated applications.
neurips-2025-avoiding-exp-r-scaling-in-r.tldr: SE-POPO replaces exponential reward-range dependence with polynomial sample complexity in online RLHF and improves feedback efficiency in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Several physical modeling tasks share a common structure: geometric information must be converted into a signal defined over a sphere. G2Sphere provides a general architecture for this mapping, with applications ranging from object radar responses to navigation. Its design connects equivariant graph neural networks with spherical convolutional networks rather than requiring a separate geometric representation for each task.

The computation takes place entirely in Fourier space. An equivariant network encodes geometry into latent Fourier features, and the model predicts coefficients describing a continuous spherical output. That output can be evaluated at any resolution. The hybrid architecture supports substantially higher frequency signals than comparable equivariant graph networks while avoiding the hand-designed geometry features previously used by purely spherical approaches.

Experiments cover radar response modeling, aerodynamic drag prediction, and policy learning for manipulation and navigation. G2Sphere improves accuracy and inference time relative to competitive baselines in these evaluations. The authors also find that equivariance and Fourier features improve sample efficiency and generalization, supporting the value of combining geometric structure with a continuous signal representation.
neurips-2025-bridging-equivariant-gnns-a.tldr: G2Sphere combines equivariant graph networks and spherical convolutions in Fourier space to efficiently predict detailed spherical signals from geometry.

paragraphs: Generating an image with a requested palette involves more than matching its overall colors. The colors also need to make sense for the content described by the text prompt. This paper targets a problem with generating an image first and recoloring it afterward: the resulting palette can fit the reference while assigning colors in semantically inappropriate ways.

SW-Guidance incorporates the reference color distribution directly into a diffusion model’s sampling process. It uses a differentiable Sliced 1-Wasserstein distance to measure the mismatch between generated colors and the reference palette. Because this measure participates during generation, color matching can influence the developing image rather than being applied only after its content has already been produced.

The approach requires no additional training. The reported evaluation finds better reference-color similarity than state-of-the-art color-conditional generation methods, while generated images retain semantic coherence with their text prompts. Its contribution is thus a way to coordinate palette control with content generation within sampling, addressing the specific mismatch that can arise when these two operations are performed separately.
neurips-2025-color-conditional-generatio.tldr: SW-Guidance steers diffusion sampling toward a reference palette without additional training while preserving coherence with the text prompt.

paragraphs: Orientation maps organize neurons according to the edge directions they respond to most strongly. Such maps have long been associated with the layered visual cortex of mammals. This paper asks whether similar organization can emerge in a visual system without that cortical structure, using the fruit fly brain as the system to investigate.

The authors combine a complete fruit fly brain wiring map with biologically grounded models of spiking neurons. They stimulate the resulting network with visual inputs at different orientations and examine responses farther along the visual pathway. This ties the simulated processing to measured connectivity while allowing the researchers to study how the network’s dynamics organize responses.

The simulations show that coherent orientation maps can emerge from dynamics constrained by the connectome. This supports the possibility that cortical architecture is not required for such organization in the modeled setting. The authors suggest that independently originating species could evolve similar visual structures. That evolutionary interpretation remains a suggestion drawn from the computational result, which concerns map formation in the simulated fly visual system.
neurips-2025-connectome-based-modelling-.tldr: A spiking model constrained by the fruit fly connectome produces coherent orientation maps, suggesting similar visual organization can emerge without a cortex.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning adapts a language model to particular tasks or domains when training it again from scratch would be too expensive. However, adaptation can use data inefficiently and cause catastrophic forgetting, where learning new material damages previously acquired capabilities. This paper introduces DEAL to address these issues within a framework for continuing to adapt a model.

DEAL combines Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, with a continuous fine-tuning strategy. Its design includes modules for retaining knowledge and adapting parameter updates. These components address two connected demands: changing the model enough to learn the current task while preserving useful knowledge from earlier adaptation. The framework is intended to maintain computational efficiency throughout that process.

Experiments across 15 diverse datasets report consistent improvements over baseline methods, including substantial gains in task accuracy and resource efficiency. These results support the potential of combining low-rank updates with explicit mechanisms for ongoing adaptation. The stated outcome is improved performance and efficiency in the evaluated settings, with knowledge retention forming a central part of the proposed design.
neurips-2025-data-efficient-adaptation-i.tldr: DEAL combines LoRA with continuous fine-tuning and knowledge-retention mechanisms, improving task accuracy and resource efficiency across 15 datasets.

paragraphs: Improving a hazy or dark image before object detection seems helpful, but the two processing stages can interact poorly. This paper investigates why restoration followed by detection can become unstable. Its analysis uses Lipschitz continuity, a way of examining how changes to inputs or parameters translate into changes in a system’s behavior.

The authors characterize restoration as producing smooth transformations, while detectors have discontinuous decision boundaries that can respond sharply to small perturbations. In a cascade, even visually imperceptible noise introduced by restoration can therefore be amplified during detection. Their analysis connects this mismatch to disrupted gradient flow and difficulties optimizing the combined system.

The proposed LROD framework incorporates restoration into the detector’s feature learning and regularizes the relationship between the two tasks during training. The authors implement it for YOLO detectors as LR-YOLO. Across haze and low-light benchmarks, they report consistent improvements in detection stability, optimization smoothness, and accuracy. The findings emphasize coordinating restoration with detection behavior, rather than judging restoration solely by the apparent quality of its output image.
neurips-2025-delving-into-cascaded-insta.tldr: LR-YOLO integrates restoration with detector training to address sensitivity mismatches, improving stability and accuracy on haze and low-light benchmarks.

paragraphs: Processing long recordings presents two related challenges for large speech-language models: long sequences are computationally expensive, and dedicated long-speech training data are scarce. FastLongSpeech addresses both by adapting models for extended inputs without requiring such a training dataset. The framework focuses on making long-speech processing practical while retaining useful performance on shorter inputs.

Its first component repeatedly fuses information to compress excessively long speech sequences into manageable lengths. Its second component trains the model on short speech at varying compression ratios. Exposure to these different levels of compression is intended to transfer the model’s existing capabilities to the compressed representations it will encounter when handling longer recordings.

The authors also introduce LongSpeech-Eval, a benchmark for evaluating long-speech understanding. Experiments report strong performance on both long- and short-speech tasks together with substantially improved inference efficiency. The important connection is between compression and adaptation: the framework both shortens the input representation and trains the model to operate across compression levels, supporting long-speech use without dedicated long-speech training examples.
neurips-2025-fastlongspeech-enhancing-la.tldr: FastLongSpeech combines iterative compression with training at varied compression ratios to process long speech efficiently without dedicated long-speech training data.

paragraphs: Sometimes each observation in a dataset is an entire probability distribution rather than a single measurement. Analyzing variation between these observations is difficult because distributions do not form a vector space. Although transformation methods exist for distributions of one variable, the paper addresses the less developed case of distributions involving multiple variables.

The authors use an invertible Wasserstein slicing transformation to represent multivariate distributions in a Hilbert space, where functional data analysis tools can be applied. This enables techniques such as functional principal component analysis and the examination of modes of variation. Invertibility is central: patterns identified in the transformed space can be mapped back into distributions that retain an interpretable meaning.

The paper also establishes convergence guarantees for Hilbert space representations under a broad class of these transformations. An application to joint systolic and diastolic blood pressure distributions illustrates the method. The contribution connects a mathematically convenient representation with a route back to the original statistical objects, allowing variation to be studied without leaving the results solely in an abstract transformed space.
neurips-2025-functional-data-analysis-fo.tldr: An invertible Wasserstein slicing transform enables functional analysis of multivariate distributions and maps discovered patterns back into interpretable distributions.

paragraphs: An agent navigating a graphical interface needs to decide what to do next while keeping track of earlier progress. GUI-Rise addresses difficulties in using that history effectively and transferring navigation skills across domains. Its framework connects structured reasoning, action prediction, and history summarization so that the same assessment can support both current and future decisions.

The reasoning component estimates progress and develops the rationale for the next action. It also informs a compact summary that can be used at later steps. Training combines supervised fine-tuning on trajectories with automatically generated labels and reinforcement learning through Group Relative Policy Optimization. Specialized rewards include a history-aware objective that links the quality of summaries to performance on subsequent actions.

Under identical training-data conditions, evaluations on standard benchmarks report state-of-the-art results, with especially strong performance outside the training domain. These findings support the proposed connection between reasoning and memory: summaries are trained for their usefulness to later navigation. The reported generalization results indicate that this integrated approach helps across the diverse interface tasks evaluated.
neurips-2025-gui-rise-structured-reasoni.tldr: GUI-Rise links structured reasoning, action prediction, and useful history summaries to improve interface navigation, especially in evaluated out-of-domain settings.

paragraphs: Discovering what visual content different brain regions respond to can be constrained by the categories researchers choose to test. This paper develops a computational approach for generating new hypotheses about visual selectivity from data. It also addresses the limited expressiveness of earlier discovery methods that rely on simple, often linear models of brain responses.

An encoder–decoder transformer uses cross-attention between brain regions and image features to learn nonlinear relationships between visual representations and brain activity. The authors then combine diffusion-based image generation with large image datasets to synthesize and select images predicted to activate individual brain parcels most strongly. These images help characterize the semantic content associated with each parcel.

The approach identifies regions with selectivity for complex combinations of semantic concepts, and the authors validate those patterns computationally within and across subjects. The brain encoder functions as a digital model for exploring hypotheses about responses. The stated findings are in silico results intended to guide future fMRI experiments, providing a way to propose and computationally test richer categories before experimental investigation.
neurips-2025-in-silico-mapping-of-visual.tldr: A transformer brain model and generated images reveal computational hypotheses about complex visual selectivity that could guide future fMRI experiments.

paragraphs: Foundation models are often adapted to generate outputs with particular desired properties. Reinforcement learning can do this by rewarding outputs that meet a chosen criterion. The paper addresses applications where a single reward is insufficient because several evaluation criteria matter, including text generation and the design of biological sequences or small molecules.

The proposed method uses an iterative fine-tuning strategy across multiple reward signals. This extends state-of-the-art reinforcement learning approaches to settings with more than one criterion for evaluating generated objects. The authors also provide a theoretical analysis offering insight into the performance of this multi-reward training procedure, connecting the algorithmic proposal with an examination of its behavior.

Experiments span text, biological sequence, and small molecule generation, reporting effectiveness relative to state-of-the-art baselines. The range of domains matters because the motivating issue is shared across different types of generated outputs: one criterion may not adequately capture what makes an output useful. The findings support iterative multi-reward fine-tuning as a general approach for incorporating several desired properties into model adaptation.
neurips-2025-iterative-foundation-model-.tldr: An iterative reinforcement learning method fine-tunes foundation models across multiple rewards, with theoretical analysis and evaluations in text and molecular generation.

paragraphs: Combinatorial optimization requires selecting a good solution while satisfying a problem’s constraints. This paper trains language models to produce solutions directly from natural-language problem descriptions. It targets the dependence of existing language-model approaches on intermediate code generation or external solver calls, aiming for a unified process across different optimization problems.

Training has two stages. Supervised fine-tuning teaches solution-construction patterns obtained from domain-specific solvers. A subsequent reinforcement learning stage explicitly considers feasibility and optimality, discouraging constraint violations while improving solution quality. This separates learning how to construct candidate solutions from further training them to meet constraints and achieve better objectives.

Across seven NP-hard problems, the tuned 7-billion-parameter model achieves high feasibility and reported average optimality gaps of 1.03–8.20%. It outperforms evaluated general-purpose language models, reasoning models, and domain-specific heuristics. These results support direct language-based optimization as an alternative to problem-specific pipelines, without requiring extensive code execution or manual architectural changes for each problem. High feasibility and small gaps describe the reported performance; they do not imply every output is feasible or exactly optimal.
neurips-2025-large-language-models-as-en.tldr: Two-stage training enables a 7B language model to directly solve seven combinatorial optimization problems with high feasibility and small reported optimality gaps.

paragraphs: In cluttered environments, the order in which a robot manipulates objects can determine whether it collides with something or blocks access to another object. OrderMind learns manipulation priorities from the spatial arrangement of the scene. The focus is on deciding a workable order while accounting for relationships that approaches overlooking spatial dependencies may miss.

The architecture combines a spatial context encoder with a module that structures priorities over time. A graph connects nearby objects using k-nearest neighbors, bringing together local geometric information. The representation includes both object–object and object–manipulator interactions. For training supervision, spatial priors guide a vision-language model to generate physically and semantically plausible orders that can then be distilled into OrderMind.

The authors introduce a Manipulation Ordering Benchmark containing 163,222 samples with varying difficulty. Evaluations in simulation and real environments report significant improvements over prior methods in effectiveness and efficiency. The results support using learned spatial relationships to make real-time ordering decisions, connecting scene geometry and robot access to robust manipulation in the cluttered settings tested.
neurips-2025-learning-spatial-aware-mani.tldr: OrderMind learns object manipulation priorities from spatial relationships, improving ordering effectiveness and efficiency in simulated and real cluttered environments.

paragraphs: Linguini evaluates whether a language model can solve linguistic puzzles using information provided in the problem itself. Its central aim is to measure reasoning without requiring prior knowledge of the particular language being tested. This makes the benchmark useful for examining how models work out unfamiliar linguistic relationships from the context they receive.

The benchmark draws on the International Linguistic Olympiad corpus and contains 894 questions organized into 160 problems across 75 languages. Most of those languages have extremely limited resources. Each puzzle supplies the information needed for a solution, so familiarity with the language is not a prerequisite for high accuracy under the benchmark’s design.

Every evaluated model scores below 25% accuracy. The strongest proprietary model reaches 24.05%, while the strongest open model reaches 8.84%, revealing a substantial gap between those groups in this evaluation. These results indicate that the supplied linguistic puzzles remain difficult for the tested systems even when the necessary evidence is present. The benchmark therefore exposes a challenging form of contextual reasoning across unfamiliar languages.
neurips-2025-linguini-a-benchmark-for-la.tldr: Linguini tests linguistic reasoning from self-contained puzzles across 75 languages, with all evaluated models scoring below 25% accuracy.

paragraphs: Groups of language-model agents can collaborate on complex tasks, but a fixed organizational structure may become inefficient as tasks change or more agents participate. This paper proposes a centralized orchestrator that directs agents according to the evolving state of the work. The aim is to make coordination itself adaptable rather than keeping the same interaction pattern throughout.

The orchestrator is trained through reinforcement learning to choose the sequence and priority of agents. This allows the collective reasoning process to change as the task develops. The paper describes the relationship as a puppeteer directing puppets: a central policy determines how individual agents contribute to the group’s ongoing problem solving.

Experiments in closed- and open-domain scenarios report improved performance with lower computational costs. Further analysis attributes the improvements to the emergence of more compact, cyclic reasoning structures as orchestration evolves. These findings suggest that effective collaboration can depend on learning an economical pattern of agent interactions. In the evaluated settings, adapting that pattern improves both the quality of collective reasoning and the resources it consumes.
neurips-2025-multi-agent-collaboration-v.tldr: A reinforcement-trained orchestrator dynamically coordinates language-model agents, improving evaluated performance while reducing computation through more compact reasoning structures.

paragraphs: Shampoo is a neural-network optimizer whose practical success relies on heuristics such as learning-rate grafting and infrequent preconditioner updates. Those choices add complexity and tuning requirements. This paper investigates what these heuristics compensate for by viewing Shampoo’s preconditioner as an approximation to full-matrix Adam and examining its components separately.

The analysis distinguishes the preconditioner’s eigenvalues from its eigenbasis, separating scaling errors from errors associated with the directions of the transformation. The authors show that grafting from Adam helps compensate for stale or incorrectly scaled eigenvalues. Correcting those eigenvalues directly removes the need for learning-rate grafting in their approach, replacing an indirect adjustment with a targeted correction.

For the eigenbasis, the authors propose an adaptive rule for deciding when recomputation is needed, motivated by a stopping criterion for a warm-started QR algorithm. Different preconditioner matrices can consequently use different update frequencies. This also enables investigation of how approximation error affects convergence. The contribution is a principled account of specific Shampoo heuristics and practical techniques toward simplifying and improving this family of optimizers.
neurips-2025-purifying-shampoo-investiga.tldr: Separating Shampoo’s eigenvalue and eigenbasis errors motivates direct scaling corrections and adaptive updates that reduce reliance on optimizer heuristics.

paragraphs: Very wide neural networks can be related to Gaussian processes, but knowing that a limit exists does not specify how accurate the approximation is for a finite network. This paper studies shallow networks trained with gradient descent and asks how closely their outputs follow the associated Gaussian approximation throughout training.

The authors derive explicit upper bounds using quadratic Wasserstein distance, a measure of discrepancy between probability distributions. Their bounds apply at any training time and show polynomial decay in approximation error with increasing network width. This gives a quantitative account of convergence, extending beyond a qualitative statement that the network approaches a Gaussian process as width tends to infinity.

The analysis also tracks how architectural quantities, including width and input dimension, influence the bound, together with the effects of training dynamics. That matters because the approximation is being assessed while the network changes through learning, not only at initialization. The result provides finite-width control for the shallow, gradient-descent-trained networks studied and clarifies how the quality of their Gaussian approximation depends on model size and training.
neurips-2025-quantitative-convergence-of.tldr: Explicit bounds quantify how trained shallow networks approach Gaussian processes as width increases, including the effects of architecture and training dynamics.

paragraphs: Actions can have spatial relationships that matter for decision-making, such as continuity between rotation angles or adjacency between tactical moves. This paper uses ring attractors, models inspired by neural circuit dynamics, to represent those relationships in reinforcement learning. The structures encode spatial information and uncertainty while organizing the neural activity used to select actions.

Actions are assigned positions on a ring, and the selected action is decoded from activity in that representation. The attractor dynamics also provide temporal filtering, helping stabilize choices during exploration. The researchers investigate both an external ring-attractor model and versions integrated into deep reinforcement learning agents, examining how this structure can participate in action selection.

On the Atari 100k benchmark, the approach reports a 53% performance increase over selected baselines and an improvement in state-of-the-art performance. The result supports the usefulness of explicitly structuring the action representation in the evaluated setting. Its significance lies in connecting spatial organization and temporal stability to learning performance, with the numerical improvement referring specifically to the baseline comparisons reported.
neurips-2025-spatial-aware-decision-maki.tldr: Ring attractors organize and stabilize reinforcement-learning action selection, yielding a reported 53% performance increase over selected Atari 100k baselines.

paragraphs: Training language models on long sequences requires storing large amounts of intermediate information for backpropagation. Even gradient checkpointing can leave memory as a major constraint. StreamBP reorganizes the backward computation to reduce storage for activations and logits while preserving exact backpropagation, addressing a bottleneck that becomes more severe as sequences grow.

The method decomposes the chain rule along the sequence dimension, proceeding layer by layer. Its implementation uses the model’s causal structure to reduce computation and accelerate the backward pass. It supports common training objectives including supervised fine-tuning, GRPO, and DPO, making the memory-saving approach relevant to several stages of language-model adaptation.

Compared with gradient checkpointing, the reported results support maximum backpropagation sequence lengths 2.8–5.5 times as large, with comparable or lower backward-pass time. The same capacity can instead support larger batches to accelerate training. The authors also develop a distributed version designed to limit communication overhead in multi-GPU settings. Together, these contributions expand training capacity by changing how exact gradients are computed and stored.
neurips-2025-streambp-memory-efficient-e.tldr: StreamBP reorganizes exact backpropagation to support 2.8–5.5 times longer sequences than gradient checkpointing at comparable or lower backward-pass time.

paragraphs: Prompt caching avoids repeating work on reused conversation content, but a cache policy that works well overall may still leave some requests waiting much longer. This paper targets tail latency: the slow end of the response-time distribution. It shows that standard Least Recently Used caching can perform arbitrarily poorly on this objective because it ignores differences in conversation lengths.

Tail-Optimized LRU makes a small modification to the eviction policy. It reallocates key-value cache capacity toward high-latency conversations by removing entries unlikely to matter for future turns. The authors prove optimality under a stochastic model of conversation dynamics. That qualification is essential: the guarantee concerns the modeled setting, while the implementation remains a simple two-line change.

On real conversations from WildChat, the method reduces P90 time-to-first-token latency by up to 27.5% and P95 latency by up to 23.9% relative to LRU. Violations of a 200-millisecond service objective fall by up to 38.9%. These findings indicate that choosing which conversations retain cache space can improve the slowest user experiences without requiring a complicated caching mechanism.
neurips-2025-tail-optimized-caching-for-.tldr: A small LRU modification prioritizes high-latency conversations, with model-based optimality guarantees and substantial reported reductions in tail response latency.

paragraphs: A numerical reward can indicate which action was better without explaining how to improve the next attempt. This paper studies natural-language feedback as a richer source of guidance for language-model agents. It addresses both sides of that interaction: producing useful critiques and teaching an agent to interpret and act on them.

Critique-Guided Improvement uses an actor that explores an environment and a critic that evaluates its behavior. The critic is trained to provide detailed assessments and actionable revisions, while the actor learns to use that feedback. The framework aims to encourage exploration of alternative strategies and help the actor avoid becoming stuck in locally attractive choices.

Experiments in three interactive environments show substantial improvements over the evaluated baselines, and the resulting actor achieves state-of-the-art performance. A small trained critic also surpasses GPT-4 in feedback quality in the reported comparison. These findings support explicitly training the feedback relationship: useful language guidance depends on both the quality of the critic’s suggestions and the actor’s ability to translate them into improved decisions.
neurips-2025-the-lighthouse-of-language-.tldr: Training an actor to use actionable critiques from a trained critic improves agent performance across three interactive environments.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action models convert visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, but their computational cost can limit control speed. VLA-Cache exploits the fact that adjacent frames during manipulation often contain similar visual information. It accelerates inference without additional training by reusing computations for visual tokens that have changed very little.

The method identifies these tokens and reuses their cached key-value representations. To protect action precision, it selectively recomputes task-relevant tokens whose information is sensitive to the environment. A further strategy varies the reuse ratio across decoder layers according to attention concentration. This makes reuse depend on both changes in the scene and which information receives emphasis within the model.

Evaluations on LIBERO, SIMPLER, and a real robotic system report up to 1.7 times faster CUDA latency and a 15% increase in control frequency, with negligible loss in task success rate. The findings show that substantial visual computation can be reused in these settings while preserving critical information for actions. The central contribution is selective reuse rather than treating every unchanged-looking token as equally safe to cache.
neurips-2025-vla-cache-efficient-vision-.tldr: VLA-Cache selectively reuses visual-token computations without training, accelerating robotic control with negligible reported loss in task success.
